elements.element: Preferred: no non-solicitation obligation binding Customer at all
elements.evidence: "neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party" — a non-solicit still binds Licensee (Customer)

elements.element: Fallback: restriction is mutual (binds both parties)
elements.evidence: "neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party"

elements.element: Fallback: scope limited to personnel directly involved in the services
elements.evidence: "who was directly involved in the performance of this Agreement"

elements.element: Fallback: period runs from the end of the individual's involvement
elements.evidence: "following the end of the relevant individual's involvement in the performance of this Agreement"
"shall not mean generally advertising job openings"
"individuals who respond to job opening advertisements or who voluntarily initiate employment inquiries"
Restriction is limited to "solicit" as defined ("affirmative recruitment specifically aimed at one or more individuals"); no hiring ban appears

reasons: The redline sits squarely at the locked fallback: mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in performing the Agreement, 12 months measured from the end of that involvement, with the pre-existing general-advertising and voluntary-inquiry carve-outs untouched and no no-hire element.
Preferred (no Customer non-solicit) is not achieved, as expected for a fallback-locked target.
Minimality holds: a single sentence replacement was necessary to change party direction, scope, duration and trigger; the definition of "Solicit" and the carve-outs were left intact.

The two official checks reporting the missing 12-month period and unsolicited-approach carve-out appear to be literal-pattern false negatives; the operative text expressly states "twelve (12) month period following the end of the relevant individual's involvement" and preserves "who voluntarily initiate employment inquiries".
No undefined terms, contradictions or dangling mechanics are introduced; reference to "Licensor and/or its Affiliates" is properly replaced by the mutual "other party" formulation.
